rules.label: Sliding Fee Discount Program
rules.quote: Sliding fees are specific to all individuals and families with annual incomes at or below 200 percent of the federal poverty line.

notes: Policy requires exhaustion of alternative payment resources including all third-party payment from insurance(s), Federal and State programs.
Patients must complete the Sliding Fee Discount Program application in its entirety.
Providing false information results in revocation of discounts and immediate repayment of full balance.
Initial application: applicant has two weeks from notification to supply additional information without application date adjustment; failure results in re-dating to date information supplied.
Renewal applications required every 12 months or if financial situation changes; failure may result in loss of eligibility.
Delinquent in renewal: notice mailed with 10 business days to submit required financial information; otherwise terminated.
Discounts based on income and family size only.

Income includes earnings, unemployment, workers' compensation, Social Security, SSI, public assistance, veterans' payments, survivor benefits, pension/retirement, interest, dividends, rents, royalties, estates, trusts, educational assistance, alimony, child support, outside assistance, and other miscellaneous sources; noncash benefits (food stamps, housing subsidies) do not count.
Applicants must provide prior year W-2, two most recent bank statements, two most recent pay stubs; self-employed require three months income/expenses detail.
Self-declaration of income only in special circumstances (e.g., homeless); self-declared patients responsible for 100% charges until management determines category.
Sliding fee schedule updated during first quarter of every calendar year with latest federal poverty guidelines.
Determination provided in writing including percentage write-off or reason for denial; if approved for less than 100% discount or denied, patient must immediately establish payment arrangements.
Option to reapply after 12 months or significant income change; look back period is lesser of six months or expiration of last application.
If patient verbally expresses unwillingness to pay or vacates premises without paying, contacted in writing regarding payment obligations.
If patient does not make effort to pay or fails to respond within 60 days, constitutes refusal to pay; hospital may explore payment plan, waiving charges, or referral for collections.
Information related to decisions maintained in shared confidential file in business office to preserve dignity.
All listed providers deliver emergency or medically necessary care and are covered by this Financial Assistance policy.
sliding_fee_discount may leave out a condition: policy also requires exhaustion of alternative payment sources and completed application
